title: Lookup coalescing and batch-stitching to reduce MQA scatter for Llama/Mistral
author: Sofia Kaplan
release_notes: Improves MQA latency by coalescing KV lookups and aligning micro-batches; reduces p99 by ~12% and increases throughput by ~18% for Llama and Mistral on tested GPU profiles. Includes heuristics for spill-to-CPU thresholds and safer fallbacks for rotary embedding misalignment.
description: Context: production traffic exposed noisy tail latency for Llama and Mistral MQA models where small micro-batches scatter KV cache lookups across GPU kernels causing suboptimal kernel dispatch and extra device-to-host synchronization. This PR introduces two complementary runtime techniques: 1) lookup coalescing — group KV read requests across micro-batches within a scheduling window so a single contiguous GPU memread services multiple tokens; 2) batch-stitching/token-stitching — align and stitch adjacent micro-batches with compatible shapes so subsequent attention kernels see larger steady work units. Motivation: reduce per-token overhead, increase kernel throughput, and avoid pathological kernel launches for mixed MQA/GQA sequences. What changed (high level): implemented a coalescing layer in the KV cache read path that accumulates small read ranges for up to configurable micro-window milliseconds and issues coalesced device reads; added micro-batch alignment logic in the batcher that optionally merges compatible requests if their rotary/position offset ranges match policy; introduced a KV-slab heuristic table per-model for MQA to select slab sizes and spill thresholds (with safety caps to prevent OOM behavior on small GPUs); added a fallback path that preserves latency SLOs by falling back to uncoalesced reads when cross-model conflicts are detected; extended tracing and metrics to surface coalesce hit/miss, stitched-batch counts, and micro-window wait times. Commits: ["Init lookup coalescing layer and tests", "Batcher: batch-stitching implementation and policy flags", "Per-model KV slab heuristic + config table", "Tracing/metrics and perf lab harness updates", "Canary rollout gating and rollback hooks", "Fix: alignment bug for rotary embeddings with odd token offsets"]. Files changed (high level): ["runtime/batcher/coalesce_batcher.cpp", "runtime/kv/kv_coalesce.cpp", "runtime/kv/kv_slab_heuristics.yaml", "runtime/kernels/dispatch_router.cpp", "sdk/benchmarks/microbench/mqa_coalesce_bench.cc", "observability/metrics/kv_coalesce.promql", "perf-canary/configs/mqa-canary.json", "tests/runtime/test_kv_coalesce.py", "docs/perf/mqa_coalescing.md"]. Tests and CI: unit tests added for coalesce boundary conditions and rotary alignment; microbench harness updated to simulate MQA conditions. CI run initially flagged a flake in the perf-canary integration test due to timing sensitivity; fixed by tightening the canary client timing and reran. Final CI status: pass on main (linux, macOS, perf-canary). Benchmarks: on our perf lab (A10g, batcher policy=aggressive, sequence len distribution sampled from customer workload) we observe median latency ~3% change, p90 ~8% reduction, p99 ~12% reduction, and sustained throughput improvement of ~18% for mixed-length MQA workloads versus baseline. Observed small regression (1.6% p50 increase) on extremely short sequences due to extra micro-window wait — mitigated by per-model policy defaults that disable stitching for seq_len<=4. Review convo highlights: Amit: asked for safety caps and rollback plan; requested additional logs for canary failure modes. Author (Sofia): added slab caps and canary gates; replied with implementation details and load-tested rollback. Priya: requested benchmark reproducibility; author added harness config and seed details. Liam: approved after nit on metric naming and one small memory-leak fix. Rollout plan: staged canary in perf-canary for 72h, then 50% traffic on Dedicated clusters with monitoring dashboards for kv_coalesce_hit_rate, stitched_batch_ratio, and p99 token latency; automatic rollback if p99 regresses >5% or memory pressure spikes >10% above baseline. Backout: feature flag at runtime to disable coalescing and stitching with immediate effect; configuration stored per-deployment. Risks and mitigations: risk of memory pressure on tiny GPUs addressed via slab heuristic caps and immediate fallbacks; risk of increased latency for very short sequences mitigated by default policy to skip stitching for short requests. Related: touches scheduling and kernel routing logic; coordinated with ENG-10021 to avoid overlapping kernel-router changes. Conclusion: merged to main via squash; shipping metrics/observability and canary gating in place to monitor impact across fleets.
